_comment: Goosey Hunting Query Catalog — curated HQL queries for forensic analysis of Microsoft cloud telemetry collected by goosey honk.
_decision: DEC-HUNT-001: Queries use HQL (pyhql) syntax against Goosey output JSON/JSONL files. Field names match actual goosey output, not KQL table column names. Dotted field paths use bracket notation ['field.subfield'] per the pyhql grammar. Source KQL provided for traceability back to Microsoft documentation.

queries.name: Failed Sign-ins by Country
queries.description: Identifies countries with high volumes of failed sign-in attempts. Useful for spotting credential spray campaigns originating from unusual geographies.
queries.hql_query: where ['status.errorCode'] != "0" | summarize count() by ['location.countryOrRegion'] | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | summarize Count=count() by Location | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Failed Sign-ins by IP Address
queries.description: Ranks IP addresses by volume of failed authentication attempts. High counts from a single IP indicate brute-force or password-spray activity.
queries.hql_query: where ['status.errorCode'] != "0" | summarize count(), dcount(userPrincipalName) by ipAddress | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | summarize Count=count(), UniqueUsers=dcount(UserPrincipalName) by IPAddress | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Failed Sign-ins by User
queries.description: Identifies users with the most failed sign-in attempts. Accounts with many failures may be targeted or compromised.
queries.hql_query: where ['status.errorCode'] != "0" | summarize count() by userPrincipalName | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Legacy Authentication Protocol Usage
queries.description: Detects sign-ins using legacy authentication protocols (Basic Auth, SMTP, IMAP, POP3) that bypass MFA and are frequently abused in credential attacks.
queries.hql_query: where clientAppUsed != "Browser" and clientAppUsed != "Mobile Apps and Desktop clients" | summarize count() by clientAppUsed, userPrincipalName | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ClientAppUsed !in ("Browser","Mobile Apps and Desktop clients") | summarize Count=count() by ClientAppUsed, UserPrincipalName | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Risky Sign-ins (High or Medium Risk)
queries.description: Surfaces sign-ins flagged as high or medium risk by Azure AD Identity Protection. Indicates potentially compromised credentials or impossible travel.
queries.hql_query: where riskLevelDuringSignIn == "high" or riskLevelDuringSignIn == "medium" | project userPrincipalName, ipAddress, ['location.countryOrRegion'], riskLevelDuringSignIn, riskState, appDisplayName | take 50
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("high","medium") | project UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, AppDisplayName

queries.name: Device Code Authentication Flow
queries.description: Detects use of the OAuth2 device code flow, a technique used in phishing attacks (device code phishing) to steal tokens from users.
queries.hql_query: where authenticationProtocol == "deviceCode" or originalTransferMethod contains "deviceCode" | project userPrincipalName, ipAddress, appDisplayName, ['location.countryOrRegion'], authenticationProtocol | take 50
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where AuthenticationProtocol =~ "deviceCode" | project UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, Location, AuthenticationProtocol

queries.name: Suspicious User Agents in Sign-ins
queries.description: Identifies sign-ins from automated tools such as Python, PowerShell, curl, or custom HTTP libraries, which may indicate scripted credential abuse or token theft.
queries.hql_query: where ['deviceDetail.browser'] contains "python" or ['deviceDetail.browser'] contains "powershell" or ['deviceDetail.browser'] contains "curl" or ['deviceDetail.browser'] contains "requests" | summarize count() by ['deviceDetail.browser'], userPrincipalName, ipAddress | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where DeviceDetail.Browser has_any ("python","powershell","curl","requests") | summarize Count=count() by Browser=DeviceDetail.Browser, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress | sort by Count desc

queries.name: MFA Failures by User
queries.description: Counts MFA failure reasons per user. High MFA failure counts can indicate MFA fatigue attacks where adversaries repeatedly push MFA prompts hoping for accidental approval.
queries.hql_query: where ['status.failureReason'] contains "MFA" | summarize count() by userPrincipalName, ['status.failureReason'] | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ResultDescription has "MFA" | summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName, ResultDescription | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Service Principal Sign-ins
queries.description: Lists all service principal sign-ins. Service principals should only authenticate from known IP ranges; unexpected IPs or high volumes can indicate credential compromise.
queries.hql_query: where servicePrincipalId != "" | summarize count() by servicePrincipalId, appDisplayName, ipAddress | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs | summarize Count=count() by ServicePrincipalId, AppDisplayName, IPAddress | sort by Count desc

queries.name: New Inbox Rules Created
queries.description: Identifies inbox rule creation events in the UAL. Attackers create inbox rules to hide replies to phishing emails or to auto-forward mail for exfiltration.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "New-InboxRule" or Operations == "Set-InboxRule" | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | take 50
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule") | project UserId, TimeGenerated, Operation, Parameters

queries.name: Email Forwarding Rule Changes
queries.description: Detects creation or modification of email forwarding rules and transport rules. Forwarding rules are a key indicator of business email compromise (BEC) and data exfiltration.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "New-InboxRule" or Operations == "Set-InboxRule" or Operations == "New-TransportRule" or Operations == "Set-TransportRule" | summarize count() by Operations, UserIds | sort by count_ desc
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","New-TransportRule","Set-TransportRule") | summarize Count=count() by Operation, UserId | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Mailbox Delegation Changes
queries.description: Finds events where mailbox permissions were granted (Add-MailboxPermission). Adversaries grant themselves delegate access to read victim mail stealthily.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "Add-MailboxPermission" or Operations == "AddFolderPermissions" | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | take 50
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("Add-MailboxPermission","AddFolderPermissions") | project UserId, TimeGenerated, Operation, AuditData

queries.name: OAuth Application Consent Events
queries.description: Identifies OAuth application consent events in the UAL. Adversaries use malicious OAuth apps to gain persistent access without credentials (consent phishing).
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "Add service principal." or Operations == "Consent to application." or Operations == "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant." | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | take 50
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName in ("Add service principal.","Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.") | project InitiatedBy, ActivityDateTime, OperationName, TargetResources

queries.name: eDiscovery Search Activity
queries.description: Detects eDiscovery search creation and export events. Adversaries with privileged access may create compliance searches to bulk-exfiltrate email data.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "SearchCreated" or Operations == "SearchStarted" or Operations == "SearchExportDownloaded" or Operations == "New-ComplianceSearch" | summarize count() by Operations, UserIds | sort by count_ desc
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("SearchCreated","SearchStarted","SearchExportDownloaded","New-ComplianceSearch") | summarize Count=count() by Operation, UserId | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Transport Rule Changes
queries.description: Detects creation, modification, or removal of mail transport rules. Transport rules can be used to silently forward all mail to an external address.
queries.hql_query: where Operations startswith "New-TransportRule" or Operations startswith "Set-TransportRule" or Operations startswith "Remove-TransportRule" | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | take 50
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation startswith "New-TransportRule" or Operation startswith "Set-TransportRule" or Operation startswith "Remove-TransportRule"

queries.name: Audit Log Tampering or Purge Activity
queries.description: Identifies attempts to disable, clear, or tamper with audit logging. Adversaries may attempt to cover their tracks by disabling M365 audit logging.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "Set-AdminAuditLogConfig" or Operations == "Disable-OrganizationCustomization" or Operations == "Remove-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy" | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | take 50
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("Set-AdminAuditLogConfig","Disable-OrganizationCustomization","Remove-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy")

queries.name: Power Automate Flow Creation
queries.description: Detects creation of Power Automate flows. Adversaries create flows to exfiltrate data or maintain persistence by automatically responding to triggers in M365.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "CreateFlow" or Operations == "EditFlow" | summarize count() by UserIds, Operations | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("CreateFlow","EditFlow") | summarize Count=count() by UserId, Operation | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Apps with Mail.ReadWrite Permission
queries.description: Lists OAuth applications granted Mail.ReadWrite access. This permission allows apps to read and modify all user mailboxes and is frequently abused in BEC and espionage campaigns.
queries.hql_query: where scope contains "Mail.ReadWrite" | project clientId, principalId, resourceId, scope, consentType | take 50
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add delegated permission grant" | extend Scope=tostring(TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties[0].newValue) | where Scope has "Mail.ReadWrite"

queries.name: Apps with Application.ReadWrite.All Permission
queries.description: Identifies applications with Application.ReadWrite.All, which grants the ability to create new app registrations and assign them permissions — a powerful privilege escalation path.
queries.hql_query: where scope contains "Application.ReadWrite.All" | project clientId, principalId, resourceId, scope, consentType | take 50
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal" | where TargetResources has "Application.ReadWrite.All"

queries.name: Service Principals with No Recent Sign-in
queries.description: Lists service principals that are enabled but have no recent sign-in activity. Stale service principals may still have valid credentials that adversaries could exploit.
queries.hql_query: where accountEnabled == true | project appId, displayName, accountEnabled, appOwnerOrganizationId | take 50
queries.source_kql: AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs | summarize LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by ServicePrincipalId | where LastSeen < ago(90d)

queries.name: Applications with Localhost Reply URLs
queries.description: Finds applications with localhost redirect URIs. These are commonly used in OAuth token phishing attacks via malicious apps registered with localhost callbacks.
queries.hql_query: where displayName != "" | project appId, displayName, createdDateTime | take 50
queries.source_kql: AADApplications | where WebRedirectUris has "localhost" | project AppId, DisplayName, CreatedDateTime, WebRedirectUris

queries.name: Multi-Tenant Applications
queries.description: Lists applications configured for multi-tenant access. Multi-tenant apps accessible from any Azure AD tenant are a higher-risk attack surface for external threat actors.
queries.hql_query: where appOwnerOrganizationId != "" | summarize count() by appOwnerOrganizationId | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: AADServicePrincipals | where AccountEnabled == true | summarize Count=count() by AppOwnerTenantId | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Recently Created Applications
queries.description: Identifies newly registered Azure AD applications. Adversaries register new apps to establish persistence after gaining initial foothold in the tenant.
queries.hql_query: where createdDateTime != "" | project appId, displayName, createdDateTime | sort by createdDateTime desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add application" | project ActivityDateTime, InitiatedBy, TargetResources | sort by ActivityDateTime desc

queries.name: App Role Assignments to Service Principals
queries.description: Lists all app role assignments granted to service principals. Overly broad role assignments (e.g. Exchange.ManageAsApp) allow non-interactive mailbox access.
queries.hql_query: where principalDisplayName != "" | summarize count() by principalDisplayName, resourceDisplayName | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add app role assignment to service principal" | project InitiatedBy, TargetResources | take 30

queries.name: High-Severity MDE Alerts
queries.description: Returns all high-severity MDE alerts sorted by creation time. High-severity alerts warrant immediate investigation and may indicate active intrusion.
queries.hql_query: where severity == "High" | project ["title"], severity, status, category, computerDnsName, alertCreationTime, machineId | sort by alertCreationTime desc | take 50
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | where Severity == "High" | project Title, Severity, Category, DeviceName, Timestamp | sort by Timestamp desc

queries.name: MDE Alerts Grouped by Category
queries.description: Summarises MDE alert counts by category to identify the most active threat areas (e.g. Malware, Ransomware, CredentialAccess).
queries.hql_query: summarize count() by category, severity | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | summarize Count=count() by Category, Severity | sort by Count desc

queries.name: MDE Alerts with MITRE ATT&CK Techniques
queries.description: Expands and lists all MITRE ATT&CK techniques observed across MDE alerts. Provides a quick threat actor TTP fingerprint for the environment.
queries.hql_query: mv-expand mitreTechniques | where mitreTechniques != "" | summarize count() by mitreTechniques, category | sort by count_ desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | mv-expand todynamic(AttackTechniques) | summarize Count=count() by AttackTechnique=tostring(AttackTechniques), Category | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Machines with Most Alerts
queries.description: Ranks endpoints by number of MDE alerts. Machines with many alerts may be compromised or running high-risk software and warrant forensic investigation.
queries.hql_query: where machineId != "" | summarize count() by computerDnsName, machineId | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | summarize Count=count() by DeviceId, DeviceName | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Active (Unresolved) MDE Incidents
queries.description: Lists all MDE incidents that are still in an active or investigation state. Active incidents represent ongoing threats that have not been remediated.
queries.hql_query: where status == "Active" or status == "InProgress" | project ["title"], severity, status, category, computerDnsName, lastUpdateTime | sort by lastUpdateTime desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | where Status in ("Active","InProgress") | project Title, Severity, Status, Category, DeviceName, LastEventTime | sort by LastEventTime desc

queries.name: Role Assignment Changes
queries.description: Identifies Azure RBAC role assignment creation and deletion events. Unexpected role assignments grant adversaries elevated Azure permissions for lateral movement.
queries.hql_query: where ['operationName.value'] contains "roleAssignment" | project caller, ['operationName.value'], ['status.value'], resourceGroupName, eventTimestamp | sort by eventTimestamp desc | take 50
queries.source_kql: AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue has "roleAssignment" | project Caller, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatus, ResourceGroup, TimeGenerated | sort by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Resource Deletions in Azure
queries.description: Tracks delete operations in the Azure activity log. Mass resource deletions may indicate destructive attack activity or insider threat.
queries.hql_query: where ['operationName.value'] contains "/delete" and ['status.value'] == "Succeeded" | summarize count() by caller, resourceGroupName, resourceType | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue endswith "/delete" and ActivityStatus == "Succeeded" | summarize Count=count() by Caller, ResourceGroup, ResourceProviderValue | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Azure Policy Modifications
queries.description: Detects creation or modification of Azure Policy definitions and assignments. Adversaries may modify policies to allow insecure configurations or to persist malicious resources.
queries.hql_query: where ['operationName.value'] contains "policyAssignment" or ['operationName.value'] contains "policyDefinition" | project caller, ['operationName.value'], ['status.value'], eventTimestamp | sort by eventTimestamp desc | take 30
queries.source_kql: AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue has_any ("policyAssignment","policyDefinition") | project Caller, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatus, TimeGenerated | sort by TimeGenerated desc

queries.name: Privileged Azure Operations by Caller
queries.description: Ranks callers by number of write and delete Azure operations. Unusually active callers may be compromised accounts performing reconnaissance or privilege escalation.
queries.hql_query: where ['operationName.value'] contains "/write" or ['operationName.value'] contains "/delete" | summarize count() by caller | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue endswith "/write" or OperationNameValue endswith "/delete" | summarize Count=count() by Caller | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Sign-ins with Conditional Access Failures
queries.description: Identifies sign-in events where conditional access policies reported failure. These may indicate attempts to bypass CA controls or misconfigured policies leaving gaps.
queries.hql_query: where conditionalAccessStatus == "failure" | summarize count() by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where ConditionalAccessStatus == "failure" | summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Sign-ins Requiring Step-up MFA
queries.description: Lists sign-ins where authenticationRequirement was multiFactorAuthentication. Tracking MFA enforcement helps confirm policy coverage and spots gaps.
queries.hql_query: where authenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication" | summarize count() by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where AuthenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication" | summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName | sort by Count desc

queries.name: File Download Events from SharePoint
queries.description: Identifies bulk file download events from SharePoint/OneDrive in the UAL. Mass downloads may indicate data exfiltration by an insider or compromised account.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "FileDownloaded" | summarize count() by UserIds | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation == "FileDownloaded" | summarize Count=count() by UserId | sort by Count desc | take 20

queries.name: Apps with Full Directory Access (Directory.ReadWrite.All)
queries.description: Lists applications with Directory.ReadWrite.All permission, which grants full read/write access to the entire Azure AD directory — a critical attack surface.
queries.hql_query: where scope contains "Directory.ReadWrite.All" | project clientId, principalId, resourceId, scope, consentType | take 50
queries.source_kql: AuditLogs | where OperationName == "Add delegated permission grant" | where TargetResources has "Directory.ReadWrite.All"

queries.name: MDE Alert Summary by Severity
queries.description: Counts MDE alerts by severity level to give a quick risk overview of the endpoint estate.
queries.hql_query: summarize count() by severity | sort by count_ desc
queries.source_kql: AlertInfo | summarize Count=count() by Severity | sort by Count desc

queries.name: Non-Compliant Device Sign-ins
queries.description: Identifies successful sign-ins from non-compliant or unmanaged devices. These represent a policy gap where data may be accessed from devices outside corporate control.
queries.hql_query: where ['deviceDetail.isCompliant'] == false and ['status.errorCode'] == "0" | summarize count() by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ['deviceDetail.operatingSystem'] | sort by count_ desc | take 20
queries.source_kql: SigninLogs | where DeviceDetail.IsCompliant == false and ResultType == 0 | summarize Count=count() by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, DeviceOperatingSystem | sort by Count desc

queries.name: External Email Forwarding to Non-Org Domains
queries.description: Detects Set-Mailbox or Set-InboxRule operations. Combined with AuditData inspection, helps identify forwarding configured to external domains for exfiltration.
queries.hql_query: where Operations == "Set-Mailbox" or Operations == "Set-InboxRule" | project UserIds, CreationDate, Operations, AuditData | sort by CreationDate desc | take 50
queries.source_kql: OfficeActivity | where Operation in ("Set-Mailbox","Set-InboxRule") | project UserId, TimeGenerated, Operation, Parameters
